canvod.store API reference¶

Versioned data storage using Icechunk.

Package¶

canvod-store: Icechunk storage for GNSS VOD data.

This package provides versioned storage for GNSS VOD data using Icechunk. Manages both RINEX observation storage and VOD analysis results, and stores hemisphere grids and the analysis results computed on them.

MyIcechunkStore ¶

Core Icechunk store manager for GNSS data.

This class encapsulates all operations on a single Icechunk repository, providing a clean interface for GNSS data storage and retrieval with integrated logging and proper resource management.

Features: - Automatic repository creation/connection - Group management with validation - Session management with context managers - Integrated logging with file contexts - Configurable compression and chunking

Note on "metadata"

This class manages two distinct things both historically called "metadata":

  • File registry ({group}/metadata/table): per-file ingest ledger tracking hashes, temporal ranges, filenames, and paths. Managed by append_metadata(), load_metadata(), backup_metadata_table(), etc.

  • Store metadata (canvod.store_metadata package): store-level provenance (identity, creator, environment, compliance). Written to Zarr root attrs by the orchestrator. See canvod-store-metadata.

chunk_encoding_for(ds) ¶

Build {var: {"chunks": (...)}} matching self.chunk_strategy.

Only meaningful at group creation -- Zarr fixes an array's chunk shape the moment it's first written, so this must be passed as encoding= on the mode="w" call, never on an append (which must match whatever shape creation already fixed).

Without this, chunk_strategies config only ever affected read-side chunking (the chunks= hint passed to xr.open_zarr elsewhere in this class) -- nothing applied it at write time, so the physical on-disk chunk shape was left to Zarr's own default, silently disconnected from config. Confirmed by grepping this file and processor.py for any encoding["chunks"] assignment: there wasn't one anywhere (2026-07-18).

A dim with a configured chunk size (e.g. epoch: 17280) gets exactly that size regardless of how much data is in this particular write -- Zarr supports writing less than one full chunk in the first call and filling the rest on later appends, which is the whole point of fixing chunk shape once at creation. A dim configured -1 (or unconfigured) gets one chunk spanning whatever this write's current size is (e.g. sid: -1 -> the full SID universe already present at creation).

List the groups that hold data, at any depth.

In a GNSS store these are the receiver groups, as :meth:list_groups gives them; in a VOD store each analysis sits below its calculator (tau_omega/canopy_01_vs_reference_01).

Repository branch to examine.

 "main"

Returns:

Type Description
bool

True if the group exists, False otherwise.

Notes

Checks membership directly against the opened root group rather than via :meth:get_group_names/:meth:list_groups -- those only enumerate top-level Zarr group keys (root.group_keys()), so for a nested group_name like a VOD analysis group, membership in that flat list is always False even when the group exists. Confirmed 2026-07-21: this previously caused every VOD write after a group's first to take the mode="w" (full overwrite) branch in :meth:write_or_append_vod_group instead of appending, silently destroying all previously-written VOD data on each subsequent write. Zarr's Group.__contains__ supports slash-separated nested paths directly, so this works for both flat GNSS receiver names (no behavior change there) and nested VOD group names (the actual fix).

preprocessing_records(group_name, start=None, end=None, branch='main') ¶

Preprocessing records in group_name's log book, without repeats.

In ingest order; rows written before the record existed give "". Each file row's record includes the steps of the group-wide rows written after it (:meth:add_group_variables): it describes the data as they are now. With start and end, only rows whose data overlap that range, without rows of files skipped as already ingested (as :meth:source_file_hashes). A group without a log book gives none.

add_group_variables(group_name, variables, step, software, branch='main') ¶

Add variables computed from the data already in a group.

For example the grid cells of every observation (canvod.ops.assign_grid_cells_in_store). Only the new variables are written; the group's other variables, its attributes, its log book and its other subgroups stay as they are. The write is staged on a temporary branch and moved to branch with :meth:promote_branch.

The log book receives one group-wide row (:data:GROUP_WIDE_ACTION) whose preprocessing record holds step. From then on, the preprocessing of the data already in the group counts as their own plus step (:meth:preprocessing_records), so a later write is accepted only if it was preprocessed with step as well, and thus carries the new variables too.

grow_day_blocks(days, *, message, branch='main') ¶

Give days a block in existing day-block groups, in one commit.

A run calls this once per batch, before reading files, for the days whose Phase 1 succeeded (ADR 0016). A day that has a block keeps it, so a block grown for a day that failed later is reused on the next run. When another commit changed the branch meanwhile and the two conflict, the growth starts again on the new tip: it rereads the epoch axis, reuses the blocks added meanwhile and grows the rest.

Merge the forks of a unit of VOD days and commit them once (ADR 0021).

forks come from session, which had no changes of its own when they were made; they hold the days the worker pool wrote (:mod:canvodpy.orchestrator.vod_phase). write_or_append_vod_groups_batch(items, branch='main', dedup=True) ¶

Write/append multiple VOD analysis groups in one fork/merge batch.

The same cross-group parallelization RinexDataProcessor uses for GNSS receiver groups (_write_receiver_batch_forked), applied to VOD analysis groups: any brand-new analysis group is created directly on its own clean session that commits alone (pre-pass) -- verified empirically (see _write_receiver_batch_forked's docstring) that Session.merge() silently drops a fork's data if the base session it merges into had its own pending uncommitted writes before .fork() was called, so new-group creation and forked appends can never safely share one session. Only groups that already exist go through the fork/merge phase; a brand-new group's pre-pass write is its entire contribution to this batch (a VOD write is exactly one dataset per group per call, unlike GNSS's many-files-per-group-per- day case, so there is never leftover data for a newly-created group to append afterward).

Fail-fast: if any group's forked write raises, no merge or commit happens for the fork/merge phase -- a partial merge would silently drop a group's data from an apparently-successful commit. A pre-pass commit that already landed before a later fork failure is safe to leave in place: the next retry's dedup check sees that group's data as already-committed and won't re-attempt it.

Performs two checks in order:

should_skip_file(group_name, file_hash, time_start, time_end, branch='main') ¶

Check whether a file should be skipped before processing and writing.

Thin public wrapper around :meth:metadata_row_exists that returns a simple (skip, reason) pair instead of a DataFrame, suitable for use in Airflow task functions as an early-exit optimization.

This method is an early-exit optimization: it avoids opening a write session for files that are already present. Pass dedup=True to :meth:write_or_append_group to make the store the authoritative final gate (runs the same check again before writing).

Checks performed (in order):

  1. Hash match — file was previously ingested (exact duplicate).
  2. Temporal overlap — incoming time range overlaps existing epochs.

Layer 3 (intra-batch overlap) is not applicable here because task functions process files one at a time.

Read from group_name's log book, in ingest order and without duplicates. Rows recording a file that was skipped as already ingested (exists is "True" and nothing was written) are ignored, so each file counts once however often it was re-run.

Used as the provenance of a dataset read back from the store for that range, e.g. the daily inputs of a VOD computation.

load_metadata_for_dedup(group_name, branch='main') ¶

{group_name}'s metadata table at the tip of branch.

Read whole the first time, afterwards only the rows committed since (:class:~canvod.store_metadata.log_book.LogBooks): a run asks for it every day, and a whole read grows with the store (ADR 0021).

batch_check_existing/check_temporal_overlaps each used to call load_metadata() independently -- two full-table reads per batch, growing with store size (confirmed against a real backfill: batch_check duration tracked metadata_rows almost exactly, ~5x over 41,597 rows). Callers needing both checks should load once here and pass the result to both via their metadata_df parameter. Returns None (not an empty DataFrame) when the group/metadata doesn't exist yet, so callers can distinguish "nothing to check against" from "failed to load" without re-attempting the load.

expire_old_snapshots(days=None, branch='main', delete_expired_branches=False, delete_expired_tags=False) ¶

Expire snapshots older than the given retention period.

Metadata-only "soft delete": rewrites ancestry so expired snapshots become unreachable from any surviving branch/tag. No objects (manifests, chunks, snapshot files) are deleted at this stage — call garbage_collect() separately to reclaim storage. Keeping this expire-only (previously it also ran GC internally) is what lets a caller run GC exactly once via maintenance() instead of twice per call.

Never invoke this automatically inside the pipeline's write path: it's an administrative operation, not safe to run casually alongside active writes. Use a generous days margin (weeks to months, not hours) so it can never touch anything from an in-flight write session.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
days int | None

Number of days to retain snapshots. Defaults to 90 (weeks-to- months cadence).

 None
branch str

Branch to apply expiration on.

 "main"
delete_expired_branches bool

Whether to delete branches pointing to expired snapshots. Matches Icechunk's own safe default: flip only deliberately.

 False
delete_expired_tags bool

Whether to delete tags pointing to expired snapshots. Do not set True if using keeper tags (create_keeper_tag) — it would delete them along with any other expired-tip tag.

 False

Returns:

Type Description
set[str]

Expired snapshot IDs.

Raises:

Type Description
FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings.

garbage_collect(days=90, *, dry_run=False) ¶

Physically delete objects no longer reachable from any branch/tag.

Only removes what a prior expire_old_snapshots() (or manual ref deletion) already made unreachable — this does not itself expire anything. Always run with dry_run=True first on a store that hasn't been GC'd before, especially one with a large accumulated backlog: there's no documented cost model for GC time/memory at scale, so a first-ever run's duration is unknown until measured.

Not safe to run casually alongside active writes — the cutoff must predate the start of any concurrently-running write session, and only one expire/GC operation should run at a time. Icechunk does have self-protection against races with new commits arriving mid-run (it restarts, bounded retries, rather than deleting something a concurrent writer needs), but that's not a substitute for a generous cutoff margin.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
days int

Objects older than this (by the same write-time semantics as expire_old_snapshots) are eligible for deletion.

 90
dry_run bool

Report what would be deleted without deleting anything.

 False

Returns:

Type Description
dict

Summary of (would-be-)deleted objects.

Raises:

Type Description
FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings, also for a dry run, so maintenance behaves one way.

maintenance_due(expire_interval_days, gc_delay_days, manifest_count_threshold=None) ¶

Determine whether scheduled expiration/GC/manifest compaction are due.

Used by canvodpy store maintain-due (a cron-safe, unattended entry point -- see processing.storage.maintenance config). The repo's own ops log (:meth:get_ops_log) is the source of truth for "when did maintenance last actually run": it is written atomically by Icechunk itself as part of the same operation, so it cannot drift the way a separate marker file could (deleted, stale-copied across hosts on a shared mount, or never written if a prior run crashed after the real operation completed but before a marker write). Confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store): a real expire_old_snapshots() call always writes an ExpirationRan entry (even when zero snapshots were actually expired -- root/tip snapshots are protected); garbage_collect(dry_run=True) does not write a GCRan entry, only a real (non-dry-run) GC does -- so a dry run correctly never counts as "GC happened" here.

GC is only ever considered due after a qualifying expiration, and never again for the same expiration -- physical deletion should lag the (reversible-in-effect) soft-delete by gc_delay_days, per the skill doc's "expire every 1-2 months, GC every 15-30 days" guidance.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
expire_interval_days int

Re-run expiration if this many days have passed since the most recent ExpirationRan entry (or if there is none yet).

 required
gc_delay_days int

Run GC this many days after the most recent expiration, once per expiration (skipped if GC already ran since that expiration).

 required
manifest_count_threshold int | None

Trigger rewrite_manifests() (manifest compaction) when :meth:dir_entry_counts's manifests count reaches this. Unlike expiration/GC, rewrite_manifests() writes no distinguishing ops-log entry -- it logs as an ordinary NewCommit, indistinguishable from a data-ingest commit -- so due-ness is measured directly from current fragmentation rather than time-since-last-ops-log-entry. None (default) always reports manifests_due=False (caller opted out via manifests_enabled=False). Returns False (not an error) if the store isn't local-filesystem-backed (:meth:dir_entry_counts returns {} for S3/GCS).

 None

Returns:

Type Description
dict[str, Any]

expire_due (bool), gc_due (bool), manifests_due (bool), last_expire (datetime | None), last_gc (datetime | None), manifest_count (int | None).

compact_manifests(branch='main') ¶

Consolidate all of a branch's fragmented manifests in one commit.

Thin wrapper over repo.rewrite_manifests(): canvodpy's write pattern (one to_icechunk() call per file within a batch, e.g. 96 fifteen-minute files/receiver-day) creates one new manifest per flush, not per commit -- a single day's ingest for one receiver can create ~96 manifests. This rewrites them back to the currently-configured splitting boundaries.

Uses commit_method="new_commit" deliberately, not "amend": amend replaces the immediately-preceding commit's own message/ metadata rather than merging with it, and _append_to_icechunk already attaches structured provenance (receiver, date, file hashes) to every ingest commit -- amending could silently clobber that. An explicit, separate, auditable commit matches the precedent expire/GC already set. Like every commit, it records software, environment and settings as commit metadata (:func:canvod.store_metadata.rewrite_manifests).

Like expire_old_snapshots()/garbage_collect(), this is an administrative operation -- never call it while a pipeline run is active against this branch (ordinary commit conflict-retry semantics apply, but a still-draining worker pool committing per-file would just make every retry lose, burning cycles for nothing).

Does not shrink on-disk manifest count by itself -- confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store, 300 commits): compaction adds a new, consolidated manifest set but leaves the old fragmented ones on disk (399 -> 401 manifests immediately after compacting); only a subsequent expire_old_snapshots() + garbage_collect() actually reclaims them (399 -> 2 in the same test). This mirrors GC's own relationship to expiration -- don't expect dir_entry_counts()['manifests'] to drop right after calling this; it drops after the next expire/GC cycle instead.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
branch str

Branch to compact.

 "main"

Returns:

Type Description
str

Snapshot ID of the compaction commit.

str

Representation string.

rechunk_group(group_name, chunks, source_branch='main', temp_branch=None, promote_to_main=True, delete_temp_branch=True) ¶

Rechunk a group with optimal chunk sizes.

Zarr arrays have a fixed chunk shape once created — writing with mode="r+" onto an existing array cannot change chunk boundaries, it can only update values within the existing grid (verified 2026-07-08: a previous version of this method used mode="r+", which silently failed to change on-disk chunking whenever the request didn't align with the current chunks). Actually changing chunk size requires a destructive mode="w" rewrite of the group, which also wipes the group's nested subgroups (metadata/ table, metadata/sbf_obs) — so this method copies that subtree back afterward via a raw recursive Zarr copy (see _copy_zarr_subtree), all on a temporary branch, before main is ever touched. The copy handles canvod-store's two-level-deep metadata/{table,sbf_obs} nesting.

Both the data read and the subtree copy are pinned to the exact snapshot captured at the start of this call. If source_branch moves before the promotion, the promotion is refused with BranchMovedError (the new commits would be dropped) and the rechunked data stays on temp_branch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
group_name str

Name of the group to rechunk

 required
chunks dict[str, int]

Chunking specification, e.g. {'epoch': 180, 'sid': -1}. A group stored in day blocks needs an epoch chunk that divides every day into whole chunks.

 required
source_branch str

Branch to read original data from (default: "main")

 'main'
temp_branch str | None

Temporary branch name for rechunked data. If None, uses "{group_name}_rechunked".

 None
promote_to_main bool

If True, move source_branch to the rechunked snapshot after writing (see promote_branch).

 True
delete_temp_branch bool

If True, delete temporary branch after promotion (only if promote_to_main=True).

 True

Returns:

Type Description
str

Snapshot ID of the rechunked data

Raises:

Type Description
ValueError

If temp_branch already exists, or a day-block group gets no positive epoch chunk.
CadenceError

If the epoch chunks would split a day of a day-block group.
BranchMovedError

If source_branch moved during the rechunk.

create_keeper_tag(receiver, yyyydoy, snapshot_id) ¶

Tag a per-(receiver, date) commit as a permanent retention keeper.

Part of the tag-based retention scheme: tagging keep/{receiver}/{yyyydoy} after each commit means a later expire_old_snapshots(delete_expired_tags=False) run can safely prune everything else while these specific snapshots stay time-travelable forever. Additive and inert on its own — creating a tag doesn't expire or delete anything.

Never raises: a tag name collision (already exists, or was previously deleted — Icechunk tag names are never reusable) is logged and skipped rather than failing the pipeline write that called this.

 required

True if the tag was created, False if skipped.

Run full maintenance on the store: expire, then (optionally) GC.

Must be invoked manually or from a separately scheduled maintenance job: never from the pipeline's own run path, and never on an automatic schedule until garbage_collect(dry_run=True) has been checked against the real store and, if using keeper tags, create_tag() cost at scale has been confirmed. GnssResearchSite ¶

High-level manager for a GNSS research site with dual Icechunk stores.

This class coordinates between RINEX data storage (Level 1) and VOD analysis storage (Level 2), providing a unified interface for site-wide operations.

Architecture: - GNSS Store: Raw/standardized observations per receiver - VOD Store: Analysis products comparing receiver pairs

Features: - Automatic store initialization from config - Receiver management and validation - Analysis workflow coordination - Unified logging and error handling

source_file_hashes_for(group_name, ds) ¶

Comma-joined hashes of the GNSS files behind ds.

ds is data read from GNSS store group group_name. The hashes come from that group's log book, for every ingested file overlapping ds's epoch range (see MyIcechunkStore.source_file_hashes), so a daily dataset built from many files lists all of them. Falls back to ds.attrs["File Hash"] when the log book has no matching rows.

preprocessing_records_for(group_name, ds) ¶

ds is data read from GNSS store group group_name; the records come from that group's log book, for the files overlapping ds's epoch range (as :meth:source_file_hashes_for).

AnalysisStorage ¶

Manage persistent storage of analysis results for dataset+grid pairs.

Storage layout inside the Icechunk repository::

metadata/{dataset_name}/{grid_name}/
├── weights/              # (ncells,)
│   ├── observation_count
│   ├── solid_angle
│   └── combined
├── filter_masks/         # (epoch, sid)
│   ├── mask_iqr
│   └── mask_zscore
├── spatial_masks/        # (ncells,)
│   ├── mask_north
│   └── mask_high_elevation
└── statistics/           # (ncells,)
    ├── obs_count
    ├── mean_vod
    └── std_vod

Store manager¶

Research site manager that coordinates RINEX and VOD Icechunk stores.

This module provides the GnssResearchSite class that manages both stores for a research site and provides high-level operations across them.

GnssResearchSite ¶

High-level manager for a GNSS research site with dual Icechunk stores.

This class coordinates between RINEX data storage (Level 1) and VOD analysis storage (Level 2), providing a unified interface for site-wide operations.

Architecture: - GNSS Store: Raw/standardized observations per receiver - VOD Store: Analysis products comparing receiver pairs

Features: - Automatic store initialization from config - Receiver management and validation - Analysis workflow coordination - Unified logging and error handling

Data store¶

StoredOverlapError ¶

Bases: Exception

A file's epochs fall on epochs a file with another hash already filled.

Deliberately not a ValueError: the run stops on it instead of skipping the file (grilling on two writers, 2026-10-15, Q11). Neither file is preferred silently; gnss_store_strategy: overwrite replaces the stored data on purpose.

BranchMovedError ¶

Bases: RuntimeError

A branch moved while work for it was staged on a temporary branch.

Promoting the temporary branch would drop the commits made in the meantime, so canVODpy refuses and keeps the temporary branch.

MaintenanceOnS3Error ¶

Bases: RuntimeError

Maintenance on a store on S3 is not supported yet (#357).

Deliberately not a ValueError: nothing records it as a failed file and carries on. A store on S3 may be written by several machines, and maintenance only knows the runs of its own machine (is_pipeline_running), so a maintenance action that changes the store is refused. A garbage-collection dry run and maintenance_due still work: they change nothing.

VodWriteItem dataclass ¶

One VOD analysis pair's write request, as passed into a batch write.

VodWritePlan dataclass ¶

A VodWriteItem after dedup-check + normalization, ready to write.

VodDayWrite dataclass ¶

One analysis pair's VOD of one day, for :meth:MyIcechunkStore.commit_vod_days.

item.cadences holds the one day and its cadence. With in_fork, the day was written into a fork of the commit's session and item.dataset holds only the result's attributes; otherwise it holds the result, which the commit writes (a group's first days: the forks were made before the group existed).

MyIcechunkStore ¶

Core Icechunk store manager for GNSS data.

This class encapsulates all operations on a single Icechunk repository, providing a clean interface for GNSS data storage and retrieval with integrated logging and proper resource management.

Features: - Automatic repository creation/connection - Group management with validation - Session management with context managers - Integrated logging with file contexts - Configurable compression and chunking

Note on "metadata"

This class manages two distinct things both historically called "metadata":

  • File registry ({group}/metadata/table): per-file ingest ledger tracking hashes, temporal ranges, filenames, and paths. Managed by append_metadata(), load_metadata(), backup_metadata_table(), etc.

  • Store metadata (canvod.store_metadata package): store-level provenance (identity, creator, environment, compliance). Written to Zarr root attrs by the orchestrator. See canvod-store-metadata.

chunk_encoding_for(ds) ¶

Build {var: {"chunks": (...)}} matching self.chunk_strategy.

Only meaningful at group creation -- Zarr fixes an array's chunk shape the moment it's first written, so this must be passed as encoding= on the mode="w" call, never on an append (which must match whatever shape creation already fixed).

Without this, chunk_strategies config only ever affected read-side chunking (the chunks= hint passed to xr.open_zarr elsewhere in this class) -- nothing applied it at write time, so the physical on-disk chunk shape was left to Zarr's own default, silently disconnected from config. Confirmed by grepping this file and processor.py for any encoding["chunks"] assignment: there wasn't one anywhere (2026-07-18).

A dim with a configured chunk size (e.g. epoch: 17280) gets exactly that size regardless of how much data is in this particular write -- Zarr supports writing less than one full chunk in the first call and filling the rest on later appends, which is the whole point of fixing chunk shape once at creation. A dim configured -1 (or unconfigured) gets one chunk spanning whatever this write's current size is (e.g. sid: -1 -> the full SID universe already present at creation).

Notes

Checks membership directly against the opened root group rather than via :meth:get_group_names/:meth:list_groups -- those only enumerate top-level Zarr group keys (root.group_keys()), so for a nested group_name like a VOD analysis group, membership in that flat list is always False even when the group exists. Confirmed 2026-07-21: this previously caused every VOD write after a group's first to take the mode="w" (full overwrite) branch in :meth:write_or_append_vod_group instead of appending, silently destroying all previously-written VOD data on each subsequent write. Zarr's Group.__contains__ supports slash-separated nested paths directly, so this works for both flat GNSS receiver names (no behavior change there) and nested VOD group names (the actual fix).

preprocessing_records(group_name, start=None, end=None, branch='main') ¶

Preprocessing records in group_name's log book, without repeats.

In ingest order; rows written before the record existed give "". Each file row's record includes the steps of the group-wide rows written after it (:meth:add_group_variables): it describes the data as they are now. With start and end, only rows whose data overlap that range, without rows of files skipped as already ingested (as :meth:source_file_hashes). A group without a log book gives none.

The results of the operations (e.g. the input sampling) may differ. In a VOD store, the records are those of the GNSS data behind each result (vod_preprocessing_record).

add_group_variables(group_name, variables, step, software, branch='main') ¶

Add variables computed from the data already in a group.

For example the grid cells of every observation (canvod.ops.assign_grid_cells_in_store). Only the new variables are written; the group's other variables, its attributes, its log book and its other subgroups stay as they are. The write is staged on a temporary branch and moved to branch with :meth:promote_branch.

The log book receives one group-wide row (:data:GROUP_WIDE_ACTION) whose preprocessing record holds step. From then on, the preprocessing of the data already in the group counts as their own plus step (:meth:preprocessing_records), so a later write is accepted only if it was preprocessed with step as well, and thus carries the new variables too.

Name Type Description Default
group_name str

variables Dataset

 required
step dict

The operation that computed them, as a preprocessing step {"op", "settings", "result"} (canvod.ops.OpResult.step).

 required

Version of each package whose code computed them.

 required

Branch to change.

 "main"

grow_day_blocks(days, *, message, branch='main') ¶

Give days a block in existing day-block groups, in one commit.

A run calls this once per batch, before reading files, for the days whose Phase 1 succeeded (ADR 0016). A day that has a block keeps it, so a block grown for a day that failed later is reused on the next run. When another commit changed the branch meanwhile and the two conflict, the growth starts again on the new tip: it rereads the epoch axis, reuses the blocks added meanwhile and grows the rest.

The log book comes back unchanged; every other metadata dataset (e.g. sbf_obs) comes back from the session's base snapshot without its epochs inside drop_ranges (the replaced data), merged in epoch order with the datasets in metadata_parts (name -> per-file datasets). A metadata dataset left without epochs is not written back. Writes into session without committing.

Raises:

Type Description
LayoutError

If the group is made of day blocks: its files are written into their day's block instead, and a whole-group write would drop its layout and block index.

commit_vod_days(session, forks, days, branch='main') ¶

Merge the forks of a unit of VOD days and commit them once (ADR 0021).

forks come from session, which had no changes of its own when they were made; they hold the days the worker pool wrote (:mod:canvodpy.orchestrator.vod_phase). Under the store's commit lock: merge them, rebase onto commits made since the session was opened, write the days not in a fork (VodDayWrite.in_fork), add a log-book row per day and commit.

LayoutError

If a day's result covers more than its one day.
(RebaseFailedError, ConflictError)

If another writer changed the same chunks first; nothing is committed.

write_or_append_vod_groups_batch(items, branch='main', dedup=True) ¶

Write/append multiple VOD analysis groups in one fork/merge batch.

The same cross-group parallelization RinexDataProcessor uses for GNSS receiver groups (_write_receiver_batch_forked), applied to VOD analysis groups: any brand-new analysis group is created directly on its own clean session that commits alone (pre-pass) -- verified empirically (see _write_receiver_batch_forked's docstring) that Session.merge() silently drops a fork's data if the base session it merges into had its own pending uncommitted writes before .fork() was called, so new-group creation and forked appends can never safely share one session. Only groups that already exist go through the fork/merge phase; a brand-new group's pre-pass write is its entire contribution to this batch (a VOD write is exactly one dataset per group per call, unlike GNSS's many-files-per-group-per- day case, so there is never leftover data for a newly-created group to append afterward).

Fail-fast: if any group's forked write raises, no merge or commit happens for the fork/merge phase -- a partial merge would silently drop a group's data from an apparently-successful commit. A pre-pass commit that already landed before a later fork failure is safe to leave in place: the next retry's dedup check sees that group's data as already-committed and won't re-attempt it.

Check whether a file already exists or temporally overlaps existing data.

Performs two checks in order:

  1. Hash match — if rinex_hash already appears in the metadata table, the file was previously ingested (exact duplicate).
  2. Temporal overlap — if the incoming [start, end] interval overlaps any existing metadata interval, the file covers a time range that is already (partially) present in the store. This catches cases like a daily concatenation file coexisting with the sub-daily files it was built from.

Check whether a file should be skipped before processing and writing.

Thin public wrapper around :meth:metadata_row_exists that returns a simple (skip, reason) pair instead of a DataFrame, suitable for use in Airflow task functions as an early-exit optimization.

This method is an early-exit optimization: it avoids opening a write session for files that are already present. Pass dedup=True to :meth:write_or_append_group to make the store the authoritative final gate (runs the same check again before writing).

Checks performed (in order):

  1. Hash match — file was previously ingested (exact duplicate).
  2. Temporal overlap — incoming time range overlaps existing epochs.

Layer 3 (intra-batch overlap) is not applicable here because task functions process files one at a time.

Deliberately excludes chunks/ (can reach millions of entries -- not cheap) and only applies to local-filesystem-backed stores; returns {} for anything else (e.g. S3/GCS) since os.scandir doesn't apply.

Read from group_name's log book, in ingest order and without duplicates. Rows recording a file that was skipped as already ingested (exists is "True" and nothing was written) are ignored, so each file counts once however often it was re-run.

Used as the provenance of a dataset read back from the store for that range, e.g. the daily inputs of a VOD computation.

load_metadata_for_dedup(group_name, branch='main') ¶

{group_name}'s metadata table at the tip of branch.

Read whole the first time, afterwards only the rows committed since (:class:~canvod.store_metadata.log_book.LogBooks): a run asks for it every day, and a whole read grows with the store (ADR 0021).

batch_check_existing/check_temporal_overlaps each used to call load_metadata() independently -- two full-table reads per batch, growing with store size (confirmed against a real backfill: batch_check duration tracked metadata_rows almost exactly, ~5x over 41,597 rows). Callers needing both checks should load once here and pass the result to both via their metadata_df parameter. Returns None (not an empty DataFrame) when the group/metadata doesn't exist yet, so callers can distinguish "nothing to check against" from "failed to load" without re-attempting the load.

expire_old_snapshots(days=None, branch='main', delete_expired_branches=False, delete_expired_tags=False) ¶

Expire snapshots older than the given retention period.

Metadata-only "soft delete": rewrites ancestry so expired snapshots become unreachable from any surviving branch/tag. No objects (manifests, chunks, snapshot files) are deleted at this stage — call garbage_collect() separately to reclaim storage. Keeping this expire-only (previously it also ran GC internally) is what lets a caller run GC exactly once via maintenance() instead of twice per call.

Never invoke this automatically inside the pipeline's write path: it's an administrative operation, not safe to run casually alongside active writes. Use a generous days margin (weeks to months, not hours) so it can never touch anything from an in-flight write session.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
days int | None

Number of days to retain snapshots. Defaults to 90 (weeks-to- months cadence).

 None
branch str

Branch to apply expiration on.

 "main"
delete_expired_branches bool

Whether to delete branches pointing to expired snapshots. Matches Icechunk's own safe default: flip only deliberately.

 False
delete_expired_tags bool

Whether to delete tags pointing to expired snapshots. Do not set True if using keeper tags (create_keeper_tag) — it would delete them along with any other expired-tip tag.

 False

Returns:

Type Description
set[str]

Expired snapshot IDs.

Raises:

Type Description
FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings.

garbage_collect(days=90, *, dry_run=False) ¶

Physically delete objects no longer reachable from any branch/tag.

Only removes what a prior expire_old_snapshots() (or manual ref deletion) already made unreachable — this does not itself expire anything. Always run with dry_run=True first on a store that hasn't been GC'd before, especially one with a large accumulated backlog: there's no documented cost model for GC time/memory at scale, so a first-ever run's duration is unknown until measured.

Not safe to run casually alongside active writes — the cutoff must predate the start of any concurrently-running write session, and only one expire/GC operation should run at a time. Icechunk does have self-protection against races with new commits arriving mid-run (it restarts, bounded retries, rather than deleting something a concurrent writer needs), but that's not a substitute for a generous cutoff margin.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
days int

Objects older than this (by the same write-time semantics as expire_old_snapshots) are eligible for deletion.

 90
dry_run bool

Report what would be deleted without deleting anything.

 False

Returns:

Type Description
dict

Summary of (would-be-)deleted objects.

Raises:

Type Description
FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings, also for a dry run, so maintenance behaves one way.

maintenance_due(expire_interval_days, gc_delay_days, manifest_count_threshold=None) ¶

Determine whether scheduled expiration/GC/manifest compaction are due.

Used by canvodpy store maintain-due (a cron-safe, unattended entry point -- see processing.storage.maintenance config). The repo's own ops log (:meth:get_ops_log) is the source of truth for "when did maintenance last actually run": it is written atomically by Icechunk itself as part of the same operation, so it cannot drift the way a separate marker file could (deleted, stale-copied across hosts on a shared mount, or never written if a prior run crashed after the real operation completed but before a marker write). Confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store): a real expire_old_snapshots() call always writes an ExpirationRan entry (even when zero snapshots were actually expired -- root/tip snapshots are protected); garbage_collect(dry_run=True) does not write a GCRan entry, only a real (non-dry-run) GC does -- so a dry run correctly never counts as "GC happened" here.

GC is only ever considered due after a qualifying expiration, and never again for the same expiration -- physical deletion should lag the (reversible-in-effect) soft-delete by gc_delay_days, per the skill doc's "expire every 1-2 months, GC every 15-30 days" guidance.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
expire_interval_days int

Re-run expiration if this many days have passed since the most recent ExpirationRan entry (or if there is none yet).

 required
gc_delay_days int

Run GC this many days after the most recent expiration, once per expiration (skipped if GC already ran since that expiration).

 required
manifest_count_threshold int | None

Trigger rewrite_manifests() (manifest compaction) when :meth:dir_entry_counts's manifests count reaches this. Unlike expiration/GC, rewrite_manifests() writes no distinguishing ops-log entry -- it logs as an ordinary NewCommit, indistinguishable from a data-ingest commit -- so due-ness is measured directly from current fragmentation rather than time-since-last-ops-log-entry. None (default) always reports manifests_due=False (caller opted out via manifests_enabled=False). Returns False (not an error) if the store isn't local-filesystem-backed (:meth:dir_entry_counts returns {} for S3/GCS).

 None

Returns:

Type Description
dict[str, Any]

expire_due (bool), gc_due (bool), manifests_due (bool), last_expire (datetime | None), last_gc (datetime | None), manifest_count (int | None).

compact_manifests(branch='main') ¶

Consolidate all of a branch's fragmented manifests in one commit.

Thin wrapper over repo.rewrite_manifests(): canvodpy's write pattern (one to_icechunk() call per file within a batch, e.g. 96 fifteen-minute files/receiver-day) creates one new manifest per flush, not per commit -- a single day's ingest for one receiver can create ~96 manifests. This rewrites them back to the currently-configured splitting boundaries.

Uses commit_method="new_commit" deliberately, not "amend": amend replaces the immediately-preceding commit's own message/ metadata rather than merging with it, and _append_to_icechunk already attaches structured provenance (receiver, date, file hashes) to every ingest commit -- amending could silently clobber that. An explicit, separate, auditable commit matches the precedent expire/GC already set. Like every commit, it records software, environment and settings as commit metadata (:func:canvod.store_metadata.rewrite_manifests).

Like expire_old_snapshots()/garbage_collect(), this is an administrative operation -- never call it while a pipeline run is active against this branch (ordinary commit conflict-retry semantics apply, but a still-draining worker pool committing per-file would just make every retry lose, burning cycles for nothing).

Does not shrink on-disk manifest count by itself -- confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store, 300 commits): compaction adds a new, consolidated manifest set but leaves the old fragmented ones on disk (399 -> 401 manifests immediately after compacting); only a subsequent expire_old_snapshots() + garbage_collect() actually reclaims them (399 -> 2 in the same test). This mirrors GC's own relationship to expiration -- don't expect dir_entry_counts()['manifests'] to drop right after calling this; it drops after the next expire/GC cycle instead.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
branch str

Branch to compact.

 "main"

Returns:

Type Description
str

Snapshot ID of the compaction commit.

rechunk_group(group_name, chunks, source_branch='main', temp_branch=None, promote_to_main=True, delete_temp_branch=True) ¶

Rechunk a group with optimal chunk sizes.

Zarr arrays have a fixed chunk shape once created — writing with mode="r+" onto an existing array cannot change chunk boundaries, it can only update values within the existing grid (verified 2026-07-08: a previous version of this method used mode="r+", which silently failed to change on-disk chunking whenever the request didn't align with the current chunks). Actually changing chunk size requires a destructive mode="w" rewrite of the group, which also wipes the group's nested subgroups (metadata/ table, metadata/sbf_obs) — so this method copies that subtree back afterward via a raw recursive Zarr copy (see _copy_zarr_subtree), all on a temporary branch, before main is ever touched. The copy handles canvod-store's two-level-deep metadata/{table,sbf_obs} nesting.

Both the data read and the subtree copy are pinned to the exact snapshot captured at the start of this call. If source_branch moves before the promotion, the promotion is refused with BranchMovedError (the new commits would be dropped) and the rechunked data stays on temp_branch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
group_name str

Name of the group to rechunk

 required
chunks dict[str, int]

Chunking specification, e.g. {'epoch': 180, 'sid': -1}. A group stored in day blocks needs an epoch chunk that divides every day into whole chunks.

 required
source_branch str

Branch to read original data from (default: "main")

 'main'
temp_branch str | None

Temporary branch name for rechunked data. If None, uses "{group_name}_rechunked".

 None
promote_to_main bool

If True, move source_branch to the rechunked snapshot after writing (see promote_branch).

 True
delete_temp_branch bool

If True, delete temporary branch after promotion (only if promote_to_main=True).

 True

Returns:

Type Description
str

Snapshot ID of the rechunked data

Raises:

Type Description
ValueError

If temp_branch already exists, or a day-block group gets no positive epoch chunk.
CadenceError

If the epoch chunks would split a day of a day-block group.
BranchMovedError

If source_branch moved during the rechunk.

maintenance(expire_days=90, cleanup_branches=True, run_gc=True, *, dry_run_gc=False, delete_expired_branches=False, delete_expired_tags=False) ¶

Run full maintenance on the store: expire, then (optionally) GC.

Must be invoked manually or from a separately scheduled maintenance job: never from the pipeline's own run path, and never on an automatic schedule until garbage_collect(dry_run=True) has been checked against the real store and, if using keeper tags, create_tag() cost at scale has been confirmed. Not safe during active writes — see expire_old_snapshots/ garbage_collect docstrings for the concurrency caveats.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
expire_days int

Days of snapshot history to keep. Default 90 (weeks-to-months cadence, not the previous 7-day default — 7 days is far too aggressive for a store under sustained daily writes).

 90
cleanup_branches bool

Remove stale temporary branches.

 True
run_gc bool

Run garbage collection after expiration.

 True
dry_run_gc bool

Pass through to garbage_collect — report without deleting.

 False
delete_expired_branches bool

Pass through to expire_old_snapshots.

 False
delete_expired_tags bool

Pass through to expire_old_snapshots. Do not set True if using keeper tags — see create_keeper_tag.

 False

Returns:

Type Description
dict

Summary of maintenance actions.

open_gnss_store(store_path) ¶

Open the GNSS store at store_path; never create it.

A run creates a site's stores when it first writes to them. Reading, branches and tags need no settings file; commits, expiring snapshots and garbage collection do. A store opened without one refuses them with a FileNotFoundError that names canvodpy config init.

Raises:

Type Description
FileNotFoundError

If no store is at store_path.

open_vod_store(store_path) ¶

A run creates a site's stores when it first writes to them. Reading, branches and tags need no settings file; commits, expiring snapshots and garbage collection do. A store opened without one refuses them with a FileNotFoundError that names canvodpy config init.

FileNotFoundError

Grid storage¶

Store hemisphere grids in an Icechunk store and read them back.

A grid is written to the grids/{grid_name} group of the store as an xarray Dataset with the cell centers, vertices and solid angles (canvod.grids.grid_to_dataset).

store_grid(grid, store, grid_name) ¶

Store grid in unified xarray format to Icechunk store.

Converts the grid to an xarray Dataset with vertex information and writes it to the grids/ group in the store.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
grid GridData

Hemisphere grid instance to store.

 required
store MyIcechunkStore

Icechunk store to write to.

 required
grid_name str

Grid identifier for storage path (e.g., 'equal_area_4deg').

 required

Returns:

Type Description
str

Snapshot ID from the commit.

Examples:

>>> from canvod.grids import create_hemigrid
>>> from canvod.store import store_grid
>>> grid = create_hemigrid(angular_resolution=4, grid_type='equal_area')
>>> snapshot_id = store_grid(grid, my_store, 'equal_area_4deg')

load_grid(store, grid_name) ¶

Load a grid from Icechunk store.

Loads the grid structure from grids/{grid_name} and reconstructs a GridData object.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
store MyIcechunkStore

Icechunk store to read from.

 required
grid_name str

Grid identifier (e.g., 'equal_area_4deg').

 required

Returns:

Type Description
GridData

Reconstructed grid instance.

Examples:

>>> from canvod.store import load_grid
>>> grid = load_grid(my_store, 'equal_area_4deg')
>>> print(f"Loaded {grid.ncells} cells")

Analysis storage¶

Persistent storage for precomputed analysis results via Icechunk.

Stores dataset+grid-specific analysis outputs in an Icechunk repository under metadata/{dataset_name}/{grid_name}/:

  • weights – per-cell weight arrays (ncells,).
  • filter_masks – per-observation statistical masks (epoch × sid).
  • spatial_masks – per-cell geometric selection masks (ncells,).
  • statistics – per-cell aggregated statistics (ncells,).

Classes:

Name Description
``AnalysisStorage``

Read / write / delete analysis metadata for a single Icechunk store.

AnalysisStorage ¶

Manage persistent storage of analysis results for dataset+grid pairs.

Storage layout inside the Icechunk repository::

metadata/{dataset_name}/{grid_name}/
├── weights/              # (ncells,)
│   ├── observation_count
│   ├── solid_angle
│   └── combined
├── filter_masks/         # (epoch, sid)
│   ├── mask_iqr
│   └── mask_zscore
├── spatial_masks/        # (ncells,)
│   ├── mask_north
│   └── mask_high_elevation
└── statistics/           # (ncells,)
    ├── obs_count
    ├── mean_vod
    └── std_vod

Path to the VOD Icechunk store directory.

Preprocessing¶

Preprocessing wrapper for Icechunk storage.

This module provides the IcechunkPreprocessor class which wraps preprocessing functions from canvod.readers.preprocessing and canvod.auxiliary.preprocessing.

IcechunkPreprocessor ¶

Handles preprocessing of RINEX-converted datasets before writing to Icechunk.

This class wraps functions from canvod.readers.preprocessing and canvod.auxiliary.preprocessing.

Note: All methods now delegate to canvod.readers.preprocessing / canvod.auxiliary.preprocessing functions. The aggregate_glonass_fdma parameter should be passed from configuration.
